_doc: Alaska needs an explicit file for one reason: the Aleutians cross the antimeridian, so its geometry spans -179 to +179 and its bounding box is not a usable map view -- the same trap as the national region. Everything else is copied from _state-template.json; when that template changes, THIS FILE MUST BE UPDATED TOO. It is the one state that does not inherit.
label: Alaska
_fitBounds_note: Frames the mainland and the Alaska Peninsula. The far western Aleutians (past -172) fall outside it; they are in the data and reachable by panning. Insets are the real answer and are not built -- see docs/geography-notes.md.

geoLevels.label: County
geoLevels._note: DEFAULT. Tiles the state and is stable across the whole range, so the timeline lives here -- the same reasoning that put Columbus on county subdivisions. The three vintages are the Alaska (2020) and Connecticut (2022) boundary eras; see docs/geography-notes.md.

geoLevels.label: Township / City
geoLevels._note: Minor civil divisions in the 29 MCD states; census county divisions elsewhere. Tiles the state either way.

geoLevels.label: City / Town
geoLevels.note: Municipal limits. Much of every state is unincorporated and belongs to no place, so blank ground here is a real gap rather than missing data.
geoLevels._note: tilesRegion false is load-bearing: rule 9 forbids pooling a rate baseline over a level that leaves population out. Rates fall back to the published state figure.

geoLevels.label: Census Tract
geoLevels._note: DISABLED by default. Tracts are redrawn every decade across THREE eras (2009 / 2010-2019 / 2020-2024) and only ~43% have a complete series, so the timeline is broken here until the crosswalk exists -- rule 3. Enable per state deliberately, knowing that; the geometry and data both build correctly, it is the SERIES that is not continuous.
